featureRequest:
This is revision 3 of 3 of a larger feature. Build only this revision.

The whole feature, as the person asked for it:
# 1a. Sidebar file explorer: browsing and root rules (and 7 more)

This request comes from a conversation with the developer about their app.
Anything marked suspected or not checked is a guess: confirm it in the code before building on it.

## What this is about
The editor feels bolted on: files can be opened from outside the app, but inside the app there is no file explorer, and the existing file picker can only be reached once the editor view is showing. The developer wants one bundled feature, built in this order: (1) a VS Code-style file explorer in the sidebar with full file operations, plus palette entries for opening a file or folder; (2) F5 runs Start all / Stop all, with a new per-terminal 'executable' flag; (3) the theme finder stops overflowing its dialog; (4) the command palette gets a mobile-first CSS pass; (5) the shared Dialog and the branch menu become responsive side panes from a jattac npm package. The side panes go last because they are the largest piece and the package has not been named or checked yet. Parts 1-4 must not depend on part 5.

## What to build or fix

### 1. 1a. Sidebar file explorer: browsing and root rules (confirmed)
Add a Files explorer section to the sidebar, next to the apps list (as a second section or a tab; the layout is up to the builder). It shows a tree that loads one directory level at a time. Click a folder to expand or collapse it. Click a file to open it through the existing editor open path, which switches the main area to the editor view; if the file is already open, focus its tab instead of opening it again. Files with editor preview kinds (images, binaries) follow the editor's existing handling.

What the explorer is rooted at depends on where the user is:
- App view: the selected app's `root` (every app definition has one, src/state/model.ts:27-31).
- Editor view, active tab owned by an app: that app's root, found with the same owner lookup the tab groups already use (ownerOf in src/state/editorGroups.ts:33-40).
- Editor view, active tab in the Misc group (a file outside every app root, for example one opened through 'Edit with Tinkerdeck' in Windows Explorer, which arrives as a launch argument at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:89 or as the 'editor-open' event at src-tauri/src/lib.rs:42-50): the file's parent folder. 'Up' climbs all the way to the drive list.
- No tab open, an active tab with no path (a new unsaved file), or the home view: the user's home folder, with 'up' to the drive list.
The root moves as the active tab changes. Changing the root never closes or changes open tabs. In the editor view the sidebar may highlight the owning app, but that is optional.

Backend: add a new Rust command that lists one directory level (name, kind file/folder, and whether it can be read). None exists today; src-tauri/src/editor_cmds.rs:26-85 only has open/new/load/save/close-style commands. Add a drive-list command for the top level on Windows (Windows has no single root; Windows is a target, see installer/tinkerdeck.iss). The listing may read any path; that matches the editor, which already opens any path (editor_open_any, src-tauri/src/editor_cmds.rs:72). A folder that can't be read shows as locked and does not raise an error.

Defaults the builder should use (proposed, the developer did not object but did not explicitly confirm): hide node_modules, .git, target and dist by default; the home view shows home folder plus drives.

Evidence:
- src-tauri/src/editor_cmds.rs:26-85 (no directory-listing command)
- src-tauri/src/editor_cmds.rs:72 (editor already opens any path)
- src/state/model.ts:27-31 (app root field)
- src/state/editorGroups.ts:9-23, :33-40 (ownerOf; files outside every root go to Misc)
- src/App.tsx:70 (single view state home/app/editor)
- src/App.tsx:507-508 (sidebar highlights an app only in app view)
- src/App.tsx:524-545 (main area ternary)
- src/App.tsx:114 (one global useEditor)
- src-tauri/src/lib.rs:42-50, :89 (external opens)
- developer answers: root follows the app owning the active tab; Misc tab roots at the file's parent folder with 'up' to drives

### 2. 1b. Explorer file operations: create, rename, move, delete, drag and drop (confirmed)
The explorer supports, for both files and folders: create file, create folder, rename, move, delete, and drag and drop inside the tree (dropping an item onto a folder moves it there). All of these need new Rust commands. No user-facing file-operation commands exist in the backend today; the only fs::rename / remove_file calls in src-tauri are internal (atomic saves at src-tauri/src/editor.rs:98, buffer cleanup at src-tauri/src/editor.rs:290).

Delete (confirmed by the developer): send the item to the Recycle Bin, after a confirm prompt. The prompt names the file or folder; for a folder it says everything inside goes with it. This needs a new dependency; no trash crate is in src-tauri/Cargo.toml. Proposed: the 'trash' crate.

Proposed rules, stated to the developer and not objected to, but not explicitly confirmed:
- If the Recycle Bin can't take the item (for example some network or removable drives), refuse the delete with a message. Never fall back to a permanent delete.
- Name clashes are refused with a clear message; nothing is silently overwritten.
- Moving a folder into itself (or into one of its own descendants) is refused.
- Renaming or moving a file that is open in a tab re-points that tab to the new path so it stays open (and its tab group is recomputed, since grouping is by path). Renaming or moving a folder does the same for every open file under it.
- Deleting a file (or folder) that has open tabs closes those tabs. If any of them has unsaved changes, the single delete confirm prompt says so; there is no second prompt.
- After any operation the affected folder level in the tree is refreshed.

Evidence:
- src-tauri/src/editor_cmds.rs:26-85 (no file-operation commands)
- src-tauri/src/editor.rs:98 and :290 (only internal rename/remove uses)
- grep 'trash' in src-tauri/Cargo.toml: no match
- src/state/editorGroups.ts:33-40 (tabs grouped by path)
- developer: 'include Creating, renaming, deleting, moving, or dragging files ... files and folders'
- developer: 'Recycle Bin, with a confirm prompt'

### 3. 1c. Palette entries 'Open file…' and 'Open folder…' (confirmed)
The file picker already exists in the editor (toolbar 'Open…', Ctrl+O, and the empty-state 'Open a file…' button, all calling openDialog), but it can only be reached once the editor view is showing. Add 'Open file…' to the command palette, reusing openDialog (src/api/editor.ts:22) and opening the chosen files in the editor view. Add 'Open folder…' too, reusing pickFolder (src/api/tauri.ts:77); it roots the explorer at the chosen folder (the exact behaviour for a picked folder relative to the automatic root rules in 1a was not discussed; the builder should keep it simple, for example a picked folder stays the root until the active tab or view changes). Ctrl+O stays as it is. The palette already has an 'Open editor' entry (src/App.tsx:378) and the top bar has an editor button (src/App.tsx:450-451); these stay.

Evidence:
- src/features/editor/EditorView.tsx:36, :65, :119 (existing picker entry points)
- src/api/editor.ts:22 (openDialog)
- src/api/tauri.ts:77 (pickFolder); src/App.tsx:285 (existing use)
- src/shared/shortcuts.ts:12-15 (global shortcut list does not include the picker)
- src/App.tsx:378, :450-451 (existing editor entry points)

### 4. 2a. Per-terminal 'executable' flag (confirmed)
Every terminal gets an 'executable' flag, on by default. The user can turn it off for any terminal (add a switch where terminals are edited). Non-executable terminals are not started or stopped by Start all / Stop all or by F5; they can still be started and stopped one by one with their own buttons.
- Add the field to the TS TerminalDef (src/state/model.ts:12-25) and the Rust TerminalDef (src-tauri/src/model.rs:10-31). In Rust it needs a serde default of true so existing configs load unchanged as executable.
- start_all (src-tauri/src/commands.rs:131-141) and stop_all (src-tauri/src/commands.rs:154-165) skip non-executable terminals.
Proposed, stated to the developer and treated as accepted (not explicitly confirmed):
- The Start/Stop button state (appButton, src/state/model.ts:126-137) counts only executable terminals, so the button always shows what pressing it will do. The app status dot (rollup, used in src/features/apps/AppHeader.tsx:13 and src/features/home/HomeScreen.tsx:59) probably should too.
- The restore-on-launch prompt (src/state/useLauncher.ts:296-299, calls startAll) skips them automatically through start_all.
- The engine's 'up' action has its own loop (src-tauri/src/engine.rs:233-246); add the same filter there, and its readiness wait must ignore skipped terminals.

Evidence:
- src/state/model.ts:12-25 (no executable field in TS)
- src-tauri/src/model.rs:10-31 (no executable field in Rust)
- src-tauri/src/commands.rs:131-141, :154-165 (start_all / stop_all iterate every terminal)
- src/state/model.ts:126-137 (appButton / rollup)
- src/state/useLauncher.ts:296-299
- src-tauri/src/engine.rs:233-246
- developer: 'by default all terminals should be executable, but we should be able to mark any ... as non-executable'

### 5. 2b. F5 toggles Start all / Stop all; refresh loses its key (confirmed)
F5 runs exactly the action of the app's Start all / Stop all button (whichever appButton shows, src/state/model.ts:135-137), which skips non-executable terminals (item 2a). F5 acts only in the app view. In the home and editor views it does nothing, even though a remembered selectedAppId exists (src/state/useLauncher.ts:66).
- The global key handler is registered once with empty deps (src/App.tsx:143-156), so it closes over its initial state. Use a ref (or correct deps) to read the current view, selected app and button state at press time.
- Keep preventDefault for F5 in all views (src/App.tsx:145-147) so it is a true no-op outside the app view. Guess, not checked: without it the webview might reload the page on F5.
- F5 is an app shortcut that terminals hand back to the window (src/shared/shortcuts.ts:49-51), so it works while a terminal has focus and never reaches the shell. That is intended.
- The matcher treats any F5 press as the shortcut whatever modifiers are held (src/shared/shortcuts.ts:39); keep or tighten as appropriate, but refresh must not be on any F5 variant.
Refresh gets no shortcut at all (developer: 'No shortcut: button and palette only'). It stays reachable from the palette 'Refresh everything' entry (src/App.tsx:375), the Utilities menu item (src/features/apps/UtilitiesMenu.tsx:67-68) and the git bar button (src/features/git/GitBar.tsx:81). Remove every place that advertises F5 as refresh: the shortcuts.ts entry and matcher (src/shared/shortcuts.ts:13, :39), the palette entry's shortcut label (src/App.tsx:375), the UtilitiesMenu <kbd>F5</kbd> (UtilitiesMenu.tsx:68), the GitBar title 'Refresh now (F5)' (GitBar.tsx:81), and the help text 'Press ⟳ or F5 to refresh now' (src/features/command-palette/CommandPalette.tsx:271). Where the Start all / Stop all button or palette entry shows a key hint, show F5. Update the tests that assert F5 means refresh (src/shared/shortcuts.test.ts:15, src/App.features.test.tsx:488, src/App.shortcuts.test.tsx:119) and add tests for the new F5 behaviour, including the no-op in home and editor views. Do not move refresh to Ctrl+R: it would take reverse history search away from the shell.

Evidence:
- src/shared/shortcuts.ts:13, :39, :49-51
- src/App.tsx:143-156 (key handler, empty deps, preventDefault at :145-147)
- src/App.tsx:149 (F5 runs refreshAll today)
- src/App.tsx:375 (palette refresh entry); src/App.tsx:386-389 (Start all only in app view); src/App.tsx:550-551 (startAll/stopAll)
- src/state/model.ts:135-137 (appButton)
- src/features/apps/UtilitiesMenu.tsx:67-68; src/features/git/GitBar.tsx:81; src/features/command-palette/CommandPalette.tsx:271
- src/shared/shortcuts.test.ts:15; src/App.features.test.tsx:488; src/App.shortcuts.test.tsx:119
- developer: 'Nothing: F5 only works in the app view'

### 6. 3. Theme finder overflows its dialog (confirmed)
Clicking the theme Find button opens the ThemeFinder inside the shared Dialog (src/App.tsx:675-679). The Dialog is at most 460px wide (src/features/apps/Dialog.module.css:10), but the finder content asks for min(640px, 80vw) (src/features/themes/Themes.module.css:97-104). The theme rows are wider than the dialog and run past its right edge; the developer also finds the picker generally ugly. Fix the width directly, independent of the side-pane work in item 5: the finder content must fit its container (for example let the dialog be wider for the finder, or make the finder fill and wrap within the available width), with no horizontal overflow on desktop or mobile widths. The cause was seen in the CSS, not on screen.

Evidence:
- src/App.tsx:675-679
- src/features/apps/Dialog.module.css:10 (max 460px)
- src/features/themes/Themes.module.css:97-104 (min(640px, 80vw))

### 7. 4. Command palette: mobile-first, desktop-aware CSS (confirmed)
The command palette stays a palette; it is NOT moved to a side pane. Give it a mobile-first, desktop-aware CSS pass only. Today it has no media queries: a fixed backdrop with 12vh top padding, a panel width of min(560px, 100%) and max-height 60vh (src/features/command-palette/CommandPalette.module.css:1-20). On a phone it should fill the width and sit near the top so the on-screen keyboard doesn't squeeze the list. The desktop look stays as it is now.

Evidence:
- src/features/command-palette/CommandPalette.module.css:1-20
- grep @media in src/features/command-palette: no match
- developer: 'exclude the command palette from migration ... only optimize for mobile first and desktop awareness'

### 8. 5. Replace modals with jattac responsive side panes (Dialog and BranchMenu) (not checked)
Replace the shared Dialog (src/features/apps/Dialog.tsx:21-22; this includes the theme finder and every other dialog that uses it) and the git BranchMenu (src/features/git/BranchMenu.tsx:20) with side panes from the developer's jattac responsive-layout npm package, which fits mobile devices better than modals. The command palette is excluded (item 4). Build this last. The package has not been named: only jattac-web-poller and jattac.libs.web.zest-tabs are in package.json today (package.json:31-32). Before building, get the exact package name from the developer and check that its published build installs cleanly and ships its CSS; an earlier plan rejected a jattac package whose build was missing its CSS (docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md:340). If the package proves unusable, stop and report; items 1-4 must ship regardless.

Evidence:
- src/features/apps/Dialog.tsx:21-22
- src/features/git/BranchMenu.tsx:20
- package.json:31-32 (no side-pane package installed)
- docs/ui-tidy-up-plan.md:340 (earlier jattac package rejected for missing CSS)

## Not part of this
- Putting the editor inside the app view (as a tab or split next to the terminals). Needs decisions on cross-app tabs and main-area layout; a separate issue for later (src/App.tsx:70, :524).
- Terminal hosts are rendered only in the app branch of the main-area ternary (src/App.tsx:583-612), so they leave the tree while the editor shows. Not checked whether this loses scrollback or other state; separate issue.
- Migrating the command palette to a side pane (explicitly excluded; it only gets the CSS pass in item 4).
- Changing Ctrl+O or the editor's existing picker behaviour.
- Any shortcut for refresh (developer chose button and palette only).

## Not settled yet (do not treat as fact)
- The exact npm name of the jattac responsive side-pane package, and whether its published build ships its CSS. Item 5 is blocked until this is known.
- Not explicitly confirmed by the developer (proposed and not objected to): the hide list node_modules/.git/target/dist; home view shows home folder plus drives; Recycle Bin failure refuses rather than permanently deleting; name clashes refused; no moving a folder into itself; rename/move re-points open tabs; delete closes open tabs with one combined unsaved-changes prompt; the Start/Stop button and status dot count only executable terminals; the engine 'up' action skips non-executable terminals.
- How 'Open folder…' from the palette interacts with the automatic explorer root rules (how long a picked root persists) was not discussed.
- Not checked: whether the webview reloads the page on F5 if preventDefault is not called.

## Requirements agreed in the conversation

The developer and the assistant already agreed these while talking. Build on them; do not ask again what they settle.

- **R1**: The app provides an Open File menu item that launches the system file picker and opens the selected file in the editor, and the editor's existing open controls remain available.
  - Done when: An Open File entry is available from the app's menu or command palette even when the editor view is not the current view.
  - Done when: Choosing Open File launches the operating system file picker.
  - Done when: Selecting a file in the picker opens it in the editor.
  - Done when: The editor's Open... toolbar button, Ctrl+O shortcut, and empty-state Open a file... button launch the same picker.
- **R2**: A file explorer is shown in the side pane and displays a tree of folders and files that the user can navigate.
  - Done when: The side pane contains an explorer area for files.
  - Done when: The explorer shows the folders and files under its root folder.
  - Done when: Clicking a folder expands or collapses it.
- **R3**: Clicking a file in the explorer opens that file in the editor.
  - Done when: Clicking a file in the explorer opens it in an editor tab.
  - Done when: The clicked file becomes the active document.
- **R4**: The side-pane explorer root follows the app the user is working in: while the user is in the app view the explorer's top folder is the selected app's root folder, and while the user is in the editor view it is the root folder of the app that owns the active editor tab, found with the same path-to-owning-app lookup the tab groups use.
  - Done when: While the user is in the app view, the explorer's top folder is the selected app's root folder.
  - Done when: While the user is in the editor view, the explorer's top folder is the root folder of the app that owns the active editor tab.
  - Done when: The user does not have to choose a root by hand when an app root is available.
- **R5**: When the active editor tab belongs to no app (the misc group), for example a loose file opened through 'Edit with Tinkerdeck' from outside every app root, the explorer is rooted at that file's parent folder and moving up climbs all the way to the drive list.
  - Done when: While the active editor tab is in the misc group, the explorer's top folder is that file's parent folder.
  - Done when: Moving up from that parent folder climbs the folder hierarchy and reaches the drive list.
  - Done when: Switching the active tab between misc files changes the explorer root to the newly active file's parent folder.
- **R6**: Pressing F5 in the app view toggles start/stop of the app instead of refreshing, by invoking the same Start all / Stop all action the on-screen button uses. In the home and editor views F5 does nothing.
  - Done when: Pressing F5 in the app view when the app is stopped starts it.
  - Done when: Pressing F5 in the app view when the app is running stops it.
  - Done when: F5 performs the same action as the Start all / Stop all button.
  - Done when: F5 toggles the whole app rather than only the selected terminal.
  - Done when: Non-executable terminals are skipped by F5, exactly as they are skipped by the button (see R11).
  - Done when: Pressing F5 in the home view or the editor view neither starts nor stops anything.
- **R7**: In the theme picker's find dialog, the theme rows fit inside the dialog and do not overflow past its right edge.
  - Done when: Opening the theme find dialog shows every theme row within the dialog's left and right edges.
  - Done when: No theme row is clipped or extends past the right edge at the dialog's normal size.
- **R8**: Modal-style popups other than the command palette are replaced with responsive side panes from a jattac layout library on npm, which fits mobile devices; the shared dialog (including the theme finder) and the branch menu move to side panes, while the command palette stays a palette.
  - Done when: The shared dialog, including the theme finder, is presented as a jattac side pane instead of a centred modal.
  - Done when: The branch menu is presented as a jattac side pane instead of a centred modal.
  - Done when: The command palette is not moved into a side pane.
  - Done when: Each side pane opens, closes, and shows its content without clipping on a narrow mobile-width viewport.
- **R9**: The explorer lets the user create, rename, delete and move files and folders, and move them by drag-and-drop inside the explorer. Deleting asks for confirmation first and sends the item to the Recycle Bin, where it can be restored, instead of removing it permanently.
  - Done when: The user can create a new file and a new folder in the explorer.
  - Done when: The user can rename an existing file and an existing folder.
  - Done when: The user can delete a file and a folder.
  - Done when: Deleting an item asks for confirmation before anything is removed.
  - Done when: After the user confirms, the deleted item is in the Recycle Bin and can be restored from there.
  - Done when: The user can move a file and a folder to another folder.
  - Done when: The user can drag an item in the explorer and drop it onto a folder to move it there.
- **R10**: The command palette stays a palette and is optimised to be mobile-first and desktop-aware, rather than being migrated into a responsive side pane.
  - Done when: On a narrow mobile-width viewport the command palette is usable and its list is not squeezed by the on-screen keyboard.
  - Done when: On a desktop-width viewport the command palette keeps its current palette layout.
  - Done when: The command palette's popup mechanism is unchanged; it remains a palette, not a side pane.
- **R11**: Each terminal has an executable setting that is on by default; the user can mark a terminal as non-executable, and non-executable terminals are not started by the Start all / Stop all action or by F5 (which calls that same action).
  - Done when: A newly added terminal is executable by default.
  - Done when: The user can mark any terminal as non-executable and mark it executable again.
  - Done when: Start all does not start terminals marked non-executable.
  - Done when: F5, because it invokes the same action, does not start terminals marked non-executable.
  - Done when: A non-executable terminal can still be started and stopped on its own with its own controls.
- **R12**: Refresh is available only from its on-screen buttons and the command palette; no keyboard shortcut refreshes.
  - Done when: The refresh buttons in the Utilities menu and the git bar still refresh.
  - Done when: The command palette's 'Refresh everything' entry still refreshes.
  - Done when: No keyboard shortcut performs refresh, and the palette entry shows no shortcut key hint.

Not part of this: Placing the editor inside the app view as a tab or split pane; noted as a possible separate issue, not agreed as part of this work.; Adding an Open folder... entry to the command palette or making it choose the explorer root by hand; proposed by the assistant but not agreed by the developer.; Changing what the app's start or stop action itself does, beyond letting the user mark individual terminals non-executable; the F5 key binding and the terminal executable flag are the only changes there.; Redesigning the theme picker beyond the find dialog's fit and the move to a side pane.; Moving the command palette into a side pane; it stays a palette, only made mobile-first and desktop-aware.; Adding a keyboard shortcut for refresh; the developer chose buttons and the palette only.

This revision builds exactly these requirements (R9 to R12):
- R9: The explorer supports create file, create folder, rename, move, delete and drag-and-drop (dropping an item onto a folder moves it there) for both files and folders. Delete asks for confirmation naming the item (and, for a folder, that everything inside goes with it) and sends the item to the Recycle Bin. If the Recycle Bin cannot take the item, the delete is refused with a message and nothing is permanently deleted. A name clash is refused with a clear message and nothing is overwritten. Moving a folder into itself or one of its descendants is refused. Renaming or moving a file that is open re-points its tab to the new path and recomputes the tab groups; the same applies to every open file under a renamed or moved folder. Deleting an item closes its open tabs, and any unsaved-changes warning is folded into the single delete confirmation. After any operation the affected folder level is refreshed.
- R10: The command palette stays a palette and receives a mobile-first, desktop-aware layout pass. On a narrow, mobile-width viewport it fills the available width and sits near the top so the on-screen keyboard does not squeeze the list; on a desktop-width viewport it keeps its current look.
- R11: Every terminal has an executable flag that is on by default, is saved with the terminal, and can be turned off or on where terminals are edited. Non-executable terminals are not started or stopped by Start all / Stop all or by F5, but can still be started and stopped individually with their own controls. The Start all / Stop all button state and the app status indicator count only executable terminals. A saved terminal that has no flag loads as executable.
- R12: Refresh is available only from the Utilities menu refresh item, the git bar refresh button and the command palette 'Refresh everything' entry. No keyboard shortcut performs refresh and the palette entry shows no shortcut hint. No menu, tooltip or help text advertises F5 as refresh. Where a Start all / Stop all control shows a key hint, it shows F5.

sliceReports.summary: Slice 1 of 5 (backend/core) of revision 3. Extended the existing Files explorer core (src-tauri/src/features/explorer/mod.rs) with the four R9 file operations as plain functions: create_item, rename_item, move_item and delete_item (delete_item_with takes an injectable Recycle Bin step). They share one validation and refusal path: empty/whitespace/over-long/Windows-invalid names are refused, name clashes are refused without overwriting, moving a folder into itself or a descendant is refused, a move between drives is refused before any file-system call, and delete only ever delegates to the Recycle Bin and refuses rather than deleting permanently. Added thin Tauri command shells in the same explorer feature (explorer_create/explorer_rename/explorer_move/explorer_delete) that run on a blocking worker; rename/move return ExplorerOp with repaths, delete returns ExplorerOp with closed tab ids. Added Store::repath_prefix and Store::close_prefix to the existing editor store (src-tauri/src/editor.rs): repath keeps unsaved buffers and re-points every open file at or under the old path (component-wise, case-insensitive matching), close_prefix closes a deleted file's or folder's tabs, binning unsaved text. Registered the four commands and made editor/model public in lib.rs for the integration tests. Added the trash 5.4.0 crate to Cargo.toml for Recycle Bin deletes. Added the executable flag to the Rust TerminalDef with serde default true and a manual Default keeping it true (R11 core model). A6 version bump (2.3.0) is deliberately left to the version-bump slices: bumping only Cargo.toml here would break the one-version-everywhere check, so all three version files stay at 2.2.0 in this slice. Tests: 17 in src-tauri/tests/explorer_ops.rs, 7 in src-tauri/tests/editor_repath.rs, and one R11 model unit test. cargo check --tests, both new test binaries, the explorer integration test, and the model/editor/config unit tests pass; cargo clippy --all-targets reports no warnings in the changed files; npm run build succeeds. Note: an accidental crate-wide rustfmt was fully reverted so only in-scope files are modified.

findings.note: Scope growth is advisory in this project, so the files were accepted into the scope. They are listed in the proof report.

findings.description: The disk mutation and the editor-store update are not atomic, so a persist failure leaves a half-applied operation: the item is renamed/moved/deleted on disk (the reloaded tree shows the new state) while the command returns 'could not be renamed/moved/deleted' and the open tab still points at the old path (or a deleted file). That breaks R9's pitfall 'the tab must be re-pointed to the new path as part of the same operation, so a tab never points at a file that no longer exists' and 'a failed operation must not leave a half-created or half-moved item behind'.
findings.evidence: explorer_rename calls rename_item on line 60 (fs::rename) and only then repath_prefix on line 64, whose `?` returns Err when Store::persist fails; explorer_move does the same at lines 84/88 and explorer_delete calls delete_item on line 108 before close_prefix on line 109. The file-system change is committed first and is never rolled back if the editor-store update then fails.
findings.note: confirmed by the whole Challenge after being built (The disk change and the editor-store update are now rolled back together. rename_and_repath (src-tauri/src/features/explorer/commands.rs:56-76) and move_and_repath (:80-100) rename/move first, then call store.repath_prefix, and on Err undo the file-system change with std::fs::rename(new -> old); Store::commit (src-tauri/src/editor.rs:185-194) also puts the in-memory entries back on a failed persist, so the tab keeps pointing at the file that still exists. delete_and_close_with (commands.rs:113-130) now snapshots the entries, saves the tab close first (close_prefix returns Err before trash is touched when the save fails), and restores the snapshot with store.restore_entries if the Recycle Bin refuses. Proven by the four new tests r9_a_rename_whose_tab_update_cannot_be_saved_is_undone, r9_a_move_whose_tab_update_cannot_be_saved_is_undone, r9_a_delete_whose_tab_update_cannot_be_saved_deletes_nothing and r9_a_refused_recycle_bin_leaves_the_item_and_its_open_tab_in_place in src-tauri/tests/editor_repath.rs:232-333; `cargo test --test editor_repath` passes 11/11, including these, with the item left at its original path and no half-applied item behind.)

findings.description: The row selection is not invalidated after an operation. Move (which has no confirmation prompt) will then silently move whatever file now sits at the stale old path: e.g. rename a.txt -> b.txt, create a new a.txt, then press Move/Delete on the invisible stale selection and the new a.txt is acted on instead of the item the user sees.
findings.evidence: `selected` (line 251) is only cleared by the effect on [resetKey, root] (lines 254-258). A rename never changes the explorer root and App.tsx now keys explorerResetKey on explorer.root, so after a rename/move within the same root `selected` keeps the pre-operation ExplorerEntry (old name/path). The toolbar Rename/Move/Delete stay enabled because they are disabled only on `!selected` (lines 332, 340, 348) and act on `selected.path`; `useExplorerOps` never clears the selection.
findings.note: useExplorerOps gained an optional onCommitted callback that fires only after a successful rename, move or delete (src/features/explorer/useExplorerOps.ts:77, :125, :138, :154), and ExplorerPanel passes clearSelection so the stale selected entry is dropped after the operation (src/features/explorer/ExplorerPanel.tsx:250-254). A create or a refused/failed operation does not report, so a still-valid selection is kept. The old pre-operation path can no longer be acted on because Rename/Move/Delete are disabled once selected is null. Proven by 'R9 clears the selection after a rename ...' (src/features/explorer/ExplorerPanel.test.tsx:427-451, asserting Move/Rename/Delete become disabled and pickFolder/api.move are never called) and 'R9 clears the selection after a delete ...' (:453-466), plus 'R9 reports a committed change after a rename ...' and 'R9 does not report a committed change after a create or a refused rename' (src/features/explorer/useExplorerOps.test.tsx:92-122); `vitest run` on both files passes 57/57.
